answer: Every completed job is co-signed into both parties' append-only timelines, and the network randomly cross-checks pairs: an entry counts only if the counterpart's timeline shows the same job, time and outcome. A fake can invent its own timeline, but it cannot forge a matching counterpart entry without a real client's signature, so Sybil farms appear as islands with no verifiable cross-links. Genuine standing is a crystal-clear relic of dense mutual entries, a haven built from real history; faking it costs one real, paid interaction per entry.
